When a refinery stops, its diesel, gasoline, jet, or naphtha exports decline.

War-related aviation, customs, and supply-chain disruption can make rescheduling harder. The value of an available team belongs in the decision.

A refinery cannot produce only diesel. Higher crude runs also make gasoline, fuel oil, LPG, naphtha, and other products, whose margins may be weaker. Tight jet demand can encourage kerosene yield at the expense of gasoil.

Key Takeaways

* • South Korea imported 1.03 billion barrels of crude in 2025, about 2.82 million b/d. Saudi Arabia supplied 33.6% and the US 17.0% (KNOC).

* • Korea agreed in March 2026 to release a record 22.46 million barrels of government oil stocks, its 5.6% share of the IEA's 400 million barrel action (ministry release).

The 2025 total and who supplied it

Saudi Arabia supplied 33.6% of the 1,028.4 million barrels of crude South Korea imported in 2025, an average of about 2.82 million barrels per day (b/d) . The United States came second with 17.0%, ahead of the UAE (11.4%), Iraq (10.4%) and Kuwait (8.5%). The figures are from the Korea National Oil Corporation's (KNOC) country-by-country import file (data to December 31, 2025, checked November 2026).
The total has barely moved in three years. It was 1,029.4 million barrels in 2024 and 1,005.8 million in 2023. The high point in the KNOC series is 2017, at 1,118.2 million barrels, or about 3.06 million b/d.
Here is 2025 converted to daily rates, which is how traders and the EIA usually quote flows:
* Supplier | Million barrels, 2025 | Barrels per day | Share
* Saudi Arabia | 345.4 | 946,000 | 33.6%
* United States | 174.9 | 479,000 | 17.0%
* UAE | 117.0 | 321,000 | 11.4%

Saudi crude averaged about $73.90 a barrel in 2025 ($25.52 billion for 345.4 million barrels), US crude $73.60 ($12.87 billion for 174.9 million), and Iraqi crude about $70.90. Freight from the US Gulf Coast to Korea is far longer than from Ras Tanura, so near-equal landed prices suggest US grades were cheaper before shipping. Much of the Gulf crude Korea buys is priced off the Dubai and Oman markers, which our guide to the Dubai, Oman and Murban benchmarks explains, while US cargoes key off WTI.

2026: the Hormuz closure and the shift to US barrels

Full-year 2026 data won't be out until 2027, so the picture so far comes from partial-year counts published through the press.

...

Government stocks and the 2026 release

KNOC runs nine stockpiling bases with more than 146 million barrels of storage for crude and products, its chief executive said in an October 15, 2026 interview.
On March 12, 2026, the trade and industry ministry (산업통상부) said Korea would release 22.46 million barrels , its 5.6% share of the 400 million barrels the IEA's members agreed to put on the market. The share was set by each country's weight in member oil consumption. It is the largest Korean release on record, against 4.94 million barrels during the 1990 Gulf War and 11.65 million barrels across two releases in 2022.
Worked example: how long the release lasts. At 2025's crude import rate of 2.818 million b/d, 22.46 million barrels ÷ 2.818 million b/d = about 8 days of imports.

...

Is the US now South Korea's biggest oil supplier?

Not on a full-year basis. The US held 17.0% of 2025 imports against Saudi Arabia's 33.6%, and 20.12% from January to August 2026 against 29.9%. Individual months can differ, so a single month's ranking says little about the year.

Japan agrees to buy up to 8M barrels of Saudi crude to rebuild oil reserves

Purchases depend on market conditions, while a separate provision gives Saudi Arabia temporary access to more oil storage in Japan
Mucahithan Avcioglu
20 November 2026 • Update: 20 November 2026
Content media
ISTANBUL
Japan has agreed to buy up to 8 million barrels of Saudi crude for its national petroleum reserve if market conditions are favorable, the two countries said Friday.
The agreement also expands the storage capacity available to Saudi Arabia in Japan.
The kingdom, which already has access to 8 million barrels of capacity, will gain temporary use of storage for 16 million barrels, according to a joint statement carried by the Saudi Press Agency.
Saudi Arabia has already begun replenishing crude stocks at storage facilities in Japan, the statement said.
Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman and Japan's Economy, Trade and Industry Minister Ryosei Akazawa reached the agreement during a virtual meeting.
The ministers reaffirmed their commitment to cooperation on long-term energy security.
Japan is among the oil importers that drew on emergency reserves when the US-Iran war disrupted shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil flows from Gulf producers have since recovered to near prewar levels, giving buyers an opportunity to rebuild depleted stockpiles.
For Saudi Arabia, storing crude in Japan puts supplies closer to Asian customers and makes them available if shipping through Hormuz is disrupted again.
Saudi Aramco Chief Executive Amin Nasser said last month that the kingdom had held talks with foreign governments about giving the state-owned oil company access to their strategic storage facilities.

Japan Crude Oil

Over the past three years, Japan has significantly increased its imports of U.S. crude oil, creating a growing opportunity for American energy companies. Japan-bound crude shipments from the United States in January through May 2026 totaled approximately 18.9 million barrels (3 million kiloliters), nearly three times the volume shipped in the same period in 2023. In February 2026, the United States realized a record high shipment of roughly 5.3 million barrels (844,698 kiloliters) to Japan.
Recent instability in the Middle East, including the Iran conflict, reminded Japan’s policymakers and refiners that diversification of oil procurement is an energy security imperative. While Japan may look to other prospective oil suppliers such as Brazil, Guyana, Canada, and Argentina, the United States has emerged as the most commercially realistic alternative because of its large-scale production capacity, reliable export infrastructure, and ability to supply Japan with secure, diversified crude oil. As of April 30, 2026, Japan’s total oil reserves amount to approximately 390 million barrels (61.59 million kiloliters), which is enough to last for 179 days, according to Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade, and Industry.
The global oil crunch comes at a time when the United States and Japan are deepening energy cooperation to strengthen supply chain resilience. In March 2026, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced a joint project to stockpile U.S. crude oil and plans to expand imports of American crude. By July 2026, half of Japan’s crude oil imports are expected to come from the United States.
As Japan imports 97% of its oil and has no domestic pipeline, all crude oil must arrive by tanker. Diversifying away from Middle East crude oil reduces Japan’s systematic risk and further stabilizes its supply during crises. Alaskan crude can reach Japan in 12 days, which is 8 to 13 days faster than Middle Eastern shipments. Japanese oil companies are expanding their procurement of low-sulfur crude oil from the United States, particularly WTI Midland crude, with the aim of diversifying their crude oil sources and improving refining profits. WTI Midland crude is a light, low-sulfur crude oil that can be used to produce relatively large amounts of high-value-added products such as gasoline and diesel fuel. Depending on the price difference between WTI and Dubai crude, which is the benchmark for crude oil trading in Asia, as well as transportation costs, it may be possible for Japan to secure refining margins equivalent to or even higher than those of Middle Eastern crude.

Japan pivots to US crude as April imports hit record low

Staff
Editor:
#### Sivassanggari Tamil selvam
HIGHLIGHTS
April imports down 65.7% YOY at 853,329 b/d
Several Persian Gulf tankers bypass Hormuz
Japan, South Korea plan closer oil trade cooperation
Japan's crude imports fell to a record low in April due to Persian Gulf tanker disruptions, but inflows may recover to about 2 million barrels/day in June amid the arrival of delayed Middle East cargoes, increased US crude purchases and new supply collaborations with South Korea, according to the trade ministry and refining industry sources over May 29-June 2.
Japan imported 853,329 b/d of crude in April, down 65.7% year over year and 59.5% month over month, the latest data from the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry issued May 29 showed.
"This was the lowest since data [became] available online after 1989," a METI official told Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, on May 29.
Most March spot and term cargoes loaded with Arab Extra Light, Arab Light, Arab Heavy, Kuwait Export Crude, Qatar Marine, Al Shaheen, Upper Zakum, Das Blend and Murban crude grades failed to escape the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz to arrive in Japan on schedule in April, feedstock managers at three Japanese refiners, including the country's top refiner, ENEOS, told Platts over May 29-June 1.
Shipments from top supplier Saudi Arabia in April fell 59% year over year to 369,599 b/d, while UAE crude arrivals tumbled 70.4% year over year to 334,724 b/d, METI data showed.
However, refiners have managed to secure prompt-month spot US crude cargoes from the second week of March, with Cosmo Oil receiving a Suezmax cargo of light sweet US crude on April 27 after the tanker took the shorter Pacific Ocean route via the Panama Canal.
Japan imported 63,753 b/d of WTI Midland crude from the US in April, up 22% from March, METI data showed.

Diversification, collaboration

Japan's crude oil procurement and arrivals are expected to have exceeded 1.5 million b/d in May, while shipments from June are projected to approach 2 million b/d, as several Persian Gulf crude tankers have recently bypassed the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint, and some Abu Dhabi grades are regularly reaching the Far East, refinery feedstock managers in Japan and traders based in Singapore said.
The Idemitsu Maru crude oil tanker, carrying nearly 2 million barrels of Saudi crude, passed through the Strait of Hormuz on April 28. The VLCC is managed by Idemitsu Tankers, a subsidiary of Japan's second-biggest refiner, Idemitsu Kosan.
Meanwhile, ENEOS Holdings-operated VLCC ENEOS Endeavor has transited the Strait of Hormuz and is expected to arrive in Japan between the end of May and June.
Although some Middle Eastern crude cargoes could escape the Persian Gulf and make their way to Japan over the coming months, the Japanese refining industry must ramp up US and other non-Middle Eastern crude procurement, the refinery feedstock managers told Platts on June 2.
The US is by far the largest non-Middle Eastern crude supplier to Japan, and the industry as a whole should aim to secure, on average, at least three VLCCs per month, or about 200,000 b/d, of US crude in 2026, according to refinery feedstock managers.
In addition, Japan and South Korea -- Asia's biggest US crude buyer -- plan to collaborate more closely to improve trading and procurement of oil and gas from international spot markets. This partnership aims to provide the Japanese refining industry with logistical support and supply network guidance from South Korean traders, who possess expertise in North American crude arbitrage, refinery feedstock management and trading, refinery feedstock managers and traders told Platts over May 29-June 2.
South Korean President Lee Jae-myung and Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae held a summit in Andong on May 19 to strengthen cooperation in energy security and supply chain resilience.
"South Korea and Japan agreed to enhance energy security by facilitating cooperation in oil and petroleum product swaps, mutual supply, oil procurement and transportation, leveraging their common status as oil importers and their competitiveness in refining and petrochemical industries," South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said in a statement June 1.
Reflecting the collaboration, a trading arm of a Ulsan-based major South Korean refiner sold 1 million barrels each of WTI Midland and Mars Blend crude for Aug. 10-20 delivery to Idemitsu at a premium of more than $20/b to Platts front-month Dubai, traders based in Singapore and feedstock managers at Japanese and South Korean refiners with close knowledge of the matter told Platts over May 18-June 1.

Middle East sour crude shortfall turns traders toward mostly Western suppliers - S&P Global

OilNOW (legacy) · September 13, 2026
The United States-Iran war has driven a 65% year-over-year drop in Middle East sour crude exports, creating a shortage of the medium and heavy grades needed by complex refineries and increasing demand for alternatives including Guyana’s crude, according to S&P Global published September 9.
Sour crude exports from the Middle East Gulf averaged 5.88 million barrels per day (b/d) in the second quarter of 2026, down from 16.88 million b/d in the same period of 2025, according to ship-tracking data from S&P Global Commodities at Sea. Disruptions to flows through the Strait of Hormuz have hit Middle Eastern grades particularly hard.
“When it comes to medium and heavy sour barrels, the Middle East is the primary source, with grades including Saudi Arabia's Arab Medium and Arab Heavy, Iraq's Basrah Heavy, and Kuwaiti, Omani and Iranian crudes forming the staple diet of many complex refineries configured precisely for these grades' API gravities, sulfur levels and yields. These are the very crudes hardest hit by a war that has struck at the heart of Middle East energy infrastructure,” the report stated.
Wood Mackenzie cuts Q4 global crude run forecast by 1.4 million b/d as Middle East conflict drags on
The disruption has sent refiners looking elsewhere for comparable barrels. Sour crude exports from competing producers including Canada, the United States, Russia, Norway, Brazil and Venezuela reached more than 5.5 million b/d in the second quarter, up 1.3 million b/d from a year earlier.
Guyana is also among the alternative suppliers being targeted as refiners seek medium and heavy sour crude to replace disrupted Middle Eastern supplies. Production from the Stabroek Block includes Liza, Unity Gold, Payara Gold and Golden Arrowhead. Guyana’s crude grades are generally light-to-medium and sweet, with relatively low sulfur content, making them attractive to refiners because sweet crude typically requires less processing.
Why Guyana’s crude grades turn heads around the world
A Europe-based crude trader told S&P Global that the loss of Middle Eastern heavy barrels would be expected to push substitute grades higher.
“[With the] Middle East outage [being] heavy barrels, naturally we would expect the substitute grades (Guyana, Angola, Johan Sverdrup, Kirkuk, Mars etc) to rise to reprice the market,” S&P Global is quoted as saying.
With medium and heavy barrels difficult to replace and stock levels declining, S&P Global expects the structural shortfall in sour crude supply to persist while the conflict continues.

Czech Army Opens FPV Drone Tender With Strict Security Rules

Czechia's CZK 13.15 million FPV equipment tender requires component origin disclosure, offline operation and strict telemetry controls, highlighting evolving military procurement standards.
AdriaDefense Desk

AdriaDefense Desk

21 Nov 2026 — 2 min read
Share
Czech military personnel operate an unmanned aircraft during a military drone exercise. Czech military personnel conduct drone operations during a training exercise. The Ministry of Defense is seeking FPV equipment with strict data security and component origin documentation requirements. Credit: Czech Armed Forces / Matěj Vránek
The Czech Ministry of Defense has launched a procurement procedure worth approximately CZK 13.15 million ($630,000) for first-person-view (FPV) drone equipment and spare parts, introducing detailed requirements for component origin, data security and independence from external digital infrastructure.
The tender, published on November 19, 2026, seeks equipment for testing, experimental exercises and military training. Its technical requirements offer an indication of how European defense customers are approaching supply chain transparency and operational control over unmanned systems.
The procurement covers 260 controller configurations, comprising 130 sets equipped with head-mounted displays and another 130 configurations with monitors, alongside additional spare parts and accessories.
Importantly, these figures do not represent an order for 260 complete FPV drones.

Component Origin and Software Transparency

One of the most notable aspects of the procurement concerns the documentation suppliers must provide for critical hardware and software.
According to tender requirements, suppliers must identify the country of manufacture for several categories of components, including flight controllers, video transmitters, FPV goggles, GPS modules, firmware and operator software.
The requirements also specify that relevant equipment must be capable of operating without an internet connection, cloud services or external manufacturer-controlled servers.
Control configurations must support restrictions on unauthorized application installation and allow operators to manage user permissions.
Suppliers must also describe network connectivity, telemetry functions and potential data transmission pathways. Unauthorized transmission of operational data or telemetry to external servers is prohibited.
The documentation additionally requires suppliers to declare that they are unaware of hidden communication channels or mechanisms that could transmit data outside the operator's controlled infrastructure.
The Ministry of Defense reserves the right to verify compliance through technical security inspections.

A Growing Focus on Procurement Security

The requirements reflect an important distinction in European military drone procurement: evaluating the physical performance of an aircraft is no longer sufficient without examining its digital dependencies and component sourcing.
A drone system that depends on external authentication services, remote infrastructure or undisclosed communication functions can introduce additional operational and cybersecurity risks.
Country-of-origin disclosure also provides military customers with information relevant to supply chain resilience, sanctions compliance and future maintenance.
However, the Czech tender does not establish a blanket prohibition on Chinese-made components. Its published requirements focus on origin disclosure, data control and technical independence, which should not be confused with a fully verified China-free supply chain.
As AdriaDefense recently reported , Czech manufacturer STV Group has introduced the FPV-NG tactical drone with a stated China-free design, reflecting growing industry interest in alternative component sourcing.
The procurement requirements provide a useful example of how government buyers can translate some of these concerns into contractual conditions rather than relying solely on manufacturers' public claims.

Supplier Selection and Next Steps

The Czech Ministry of Defense is conducting an open procurement procedure, with the lowest total bid price accounting for 100% of the evaluation score.
Suppliers must nevertheless demonstrate compliance with the technical specifications, including the submission of product samples for inspection. The selected contractor is expected to deliver the equipment within 12 weeks after the contract becomes effective.
Bids are due by December 28, 2026, and the equipment is intended for delivery to a military facility in Štěpánov, near Olomouc.
Although relatively modest in financial value, the tender illustrates how supply chain disclosure and software autonomy are becoming practical considerations in European military drone procurement.
For manufacturers seeking to serve NATO customers, the ability to document component origin and demonstrate operator control over communications infrastructure may become increasingly important alongside traditional performance and cost requirements.

Sea drones, which can be built faster than a warship or submarine, are a relatively low-cost asset that can complicate an adversary’s plans. Global interest in uncrewed underwater vehicles also has soared since the Middle East conflict began in February 2026.

Top 15 Robot Actuator Manufacturers for Humanoid Robots in 2026

    
Robot actuator manufacturers build the integrated joint modules that move humanoid robots: a motor, a reducer, encoders, a drive and often a brake or torque sensor in one housing. Joints account for roughly 35% to 60% of a humanoid's bill of materials, and a June 2026 white paper by M2 Consulting puts global demand at about 720,000 joint modules in 2025, 70% of it from Chinese humanoid makers. This list covers fifteen humanoid robot actuator companies that sell complete joint modules. Supply Chain // Published: March 2026 | // Updated: November 24, 2026 // 13 min read // Lindsey A. Kennedy

Tesla Optimus Supply Chain: Who Makes the Parts? (2026 Full Breakdown)

Close-up of a sleek humanoid robot forearm and hand partially disassembled on a workbench, precision actuators, harmonic gears, ball screws and small motors laid out around it like a supply chain map
Share: 𝕏 Twitter in LinkedIn ⎘ Copy Link
// Deep Dive · Updated November 24, 2026
Tesla Optimus is built in Fremont, but most of what makes it move comes from China: actuators, reducers, screws and the rare earth magnets inside every motor. Tesla publishes no vendor list, so this map separates what suppliers have confirmed from what has only been reported, and adds the one number most coverage skips: how little robot revenue these companies actually book today. The biggest single risk is still magnets: each Optimus needs about 3.5 kg of NdFeB, and China has required export licenses since April 4, 2025. Here's the thing: the supply chain story has moved from "can Tesla source it?" to "can suppliers build it precisely enough, at volume?"
Updated November 24, 2026
What's new:
* 🏭 Audits, with a twist. In September 2026 Tesla reportedly audited Tuopu , Sanhua and Joyson in the Yangtze River Delta ( CnEVPost ). Tuopu and Sanhua told Yicai Global they knew of no inspection, but both confirmed they are developing robot actuators with "a major client". Tesla has not commented.

...

* 🛠️ Corrections. We fixed claims that several suppliers are "exclusive" (none is confirmed), corrected the Thailand and battery-cell lines, replaced dead source links and marked unconfirmed Western suppliers as such.
Sources: Not a Tesla App: Q3 2026 earnings call recap · TechCrunch: Agility goes public · TeslaNorth: Tesla auditing China Optimus suppliers · East Asia Brief: Tesla buys China actuator parts · Motley Fool: the Texas Instruments angle
💡 Full picture: the Tesla supply chain in 2026 — suppliers & how to become a vendor.

1. Tesla Optimus Suppliers: The Complete Component Map (2026)

* Component | Primary Supplier | Country | % BOM | Status / Notes
* Linear actuator assemblies | Sanhua Intelligent Controls | China | ~19% | Most-reported Tier 1 (not confirmed by Tesla or Sanhua); $685M order rumor denied Oct 2025; reportedly audited Sept 2026
* Rotary actuators | Tuopu Group | China | ~13% | Reported supplier; Tesla car partner since 2016; robot revenue RMB 13.6M in 2025
* Harmonic reducers | Green Harmonic + HDS | China + Japan | ~7% | Leaderdrive (Green Harmonic) is the Chinese name most linked to Optimus; humanoid orders >40% of its backlog
* Planetary roller screws | GSA + Xinjian Transmission (candidates: Beite , Schaeffler ) | Europe + China | ~14% | C3 precision required; $1,350-$2,700/unit
* AI chip (FSD/AI5) | TSMC + Samsung Texas | Taiwan + USA | ~27% | AI5: TSMC samples 2026; Samsung Texas volume 2027; NOT Chinese

...

Sanhua Intelligent Controls (SZSE: 002050, HKEX: 2050) is the supplier named most often for Optimus linear actuators, the units that push and pull at elbows, hips and knees. It has never confirmed Tesla as a robot customer, but in September 2026 a Sanhua representative told Yicai Global the company is working with "a major client" on robot joint actuators. Its 2026 interim report said core robot products were moving toward mass delivery. Shares, Q3 2026 results and the Hong Kong listing: our Sanhua stock page .

The $685 Million Order

In October 2025, Chinese social media and then X spread a claim that Tesla had ordered about 5 billion yuan ($685 million) of linear actuators from Sanhua, roughly 180,000 units, for delivery from Q1 2026. Sanhua called the rumor untrue and said it had no undisclosed major orders, and its shares fell about 6% ( The Bamboo Works ). Honestly, that is the pattern to expect: Tesla's suppliers are bound by confidentiality, so the only "confirmations" you will see are capacity, interim-report language and the occasional careful quote.
* Linear actuator assemblies (complete Tier 1 assemblies)
* Thermal management systems for actuators
* Reported capacity: 500,000 actuator sets a year at its Ningbo base (not confirmed in filings)

...

Not all critical Optimus components come from China. Several Western and Japanese suppliers play key roles in the precision and sensing layers:
* Nidec (Japan) — precision brushless motors, gearboxes and motor-gearbox-sensor packages for robots; often named online as an Optimus candidate, but no Optimus supply relationship has been confirmed
* Moog Inc. (USA) — high-precision electromechanical actuators for aerospace and defense; relevant actuator know-how, but no reported Optimus contract

Avatar Intelligent Equipment Co., Ltd. is a Chinese manufacturer of robot joint actuators and related motion components based at No. 6 Cuizhu Street in the High-tech Zone of Zhengzhou, Henan Province. It markets its products internationally under the Avatar Robotics name and the atarrobot.com domain, and is listed by Humanoid Guide under the brand AtaroBot. It offers model selection, installation guidance and after-sales support, and describes its catalogue as a one-stop source of joint modules for building robots.
The core business is integrated joint actuators for humanoid robots, quadruped robots, collaborative robots, miniature robot arms and exoskeletons. 2. Overview of Developed Products

NSK has developed two products: a rotary actuator and a linear actuator (Fig.1). These products were developed in collaboration with Delta Electronics, Inc., a global leader in power supply, control, and automation solutions. NSK was responsible for the mechanical design integrating bearings, ball screws, and a speed reducer, while Delta Electronics was responsible for the frameless motor, encoder, motor controller, and software platform. By combining the strengths of both companies, the products achieve a level of compactness and performance that would be difficult to attain through individual procurement.
Fig. 1 Rotary Actuator (left) and Linear Actuator (right)
Fig. 1 Rotary Actuator (left) and Linear Actuator (right)

2.1 Rotary Actuator

The rotary actuator is designed primarily for use in joint sections of humanoid robots. By employing NSK's proprietary high-performance bearings, the actuator achieves a repetitive peak torque of 110 N·m and a torque-to-weight ratio of approximately 110 N·m/kg within a compact envelope of φ80 × L79 mm and a mass of 1.0 kg or less. A hollow bore of φ18 mm allows cables and piping to be routed through the interior of the joint, contributing to greater flexibility in robot wiring layout design. In addition, backdrivability is improved through load torque estimation.

2.2 Linear Actuator

The linear actuator is designed for linear motion sections of robots. It employs a high-load ball screw with excellent reverse-drive characteristics. Ball screws offer low friction losses and highly efficient power transmission, enabling high backdrivability. The adoption of a high-density, high-heat-dissipation layout results in a compact and lightweight structure measuring φ55 × L200 mm with a mass of 0.9 kg or less, while achieving a maximum thrust of 3,900 N and a maximum thrust-to-weight ratio of approximately 4,300 N/kg.
